candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed pp.38-39: provide client education about medications; review pertinent data and medication risks; evaluate client response and take action regarding adverse medication outcomes.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — ACE-inhibitor fetal toxicity and medication safety action
candidate.educational_objective: Respond promptly to pregnancy detected during lisinopril therapy because current labeling directs discontinuation as soon as pregnancy is detected due to fetal toxicity risk from renin-angiotensin system drugs.

options.A: Continue lisinopril until the second trimester because fetal toxicity is not a concern early in pregnancy.
options.B: Notify the prescriber promptly because current labeling directs discontinuation of lisinopril as soon as pregnancy is detected.
options.C: Reduce the lisinopril dose and continue it because lower exposure removes the fetal toxicity risk.
options.D: Continue lisinopril if blood pressure is controlled because stable maternal pressure prevents fetal toxicity.

candidate.rationale: The current lisinopril boxed warning and Warnings and Precautions §5.1 state that lisinopril should be discontinued as soon as pregnancy is detected because drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. Therefore the nurse should promptly notify the prescriber so therapy can be changed in accordance with the warning. A incorrectly delays action, while C and D assume that dose reduction or controlled blood pressure eliminates the labeled fetal risk.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Pregnancy detected during lisinopril therapy requires prompt medication review because the label directs discontinuation as soon as pregnancy is detected due to fetal toxicity risk.
candidate.source_locator: Boxed Warning — Fetal Toxicity and Warnings and Precautions §5.1: when pregnancy is detected, discontinue lisinopril as soon as possible; drugs acting directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus.
candidate.stem: A client taking lisinopril reports a newly confirmed pregnancy. Which nursing action is most appropriate?
